newsitem.title: UK: Tarmac sees UK markets stable or growing.
newsitem.headline: Tarmac sees UK markets stable or growing.

text.p: British heavy building materials and construction services group Tarmac Plc said on Tuesday it expected its British markets to stabilise or grow slightly from present levels this year.
The company said in a statement that the rate of growth in U.S. markets could start to level off in 1997.
Tarmac said it was aiming to improve cash returns on investment and profit margins this year.
The company said the British construction market improved modestly in 1996, particularly in the regional building sector.
Tarmac prices for quarry products rose by between two and five percent but demand remained at low levels and sales volumes on a like-for-like basis fell by between five and 16 percent.
Construction orders totalled 1,250 million pounds at the end of the year, including secured turnover of 947 million for 1997.

Tarmac said its construction services business performed in line with expectations, excluding professional services. The latter continued to face difficulties and results were overall below expectations, Tarmac said.
However, the construction management business Schal performed well in a strengthened market, Tarmac said.
Tarmac said net debt was reduced in the second half of last year and by December 31 was "significantly" less than the half-year position of 511.6 million pounds.
